summary: India runs one of the world's largest eVisa programmes: citizens of around 170 countries can apply online for tourist eVisas valid 30 days, 1 year or 5 years, starting at 25 USD. Applications go exclusively through the official indianvisaonline.gov.in portal.

Multiple entries; 180-day cumulative stay per calendar year.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival and have at least 2 blank pages.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Travellers arriving within 6 days from a yellow fever risk country (or transiting one for over 12 hours) must carry an ICVP certificate. Without it you can be quarantined for up to 6 days — India enforces this strictly.

vaccinations.name: Polio (OPV/IPV)
vaccinations.text: Travellers from polio-affected countries (including Pakistan, Afghanistan and Nigeria) must carry proof of oral polio vaccination taken at least 4 weeks before travel.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but is strongly recommended — private hospitals require upfront payment or insurance.

onwardTicket.text: eVisa applicants must hold a return or onward ticket and sufficient funds for the stay.

proofOfFunds.text: You must have sufficient money to support yourself during the stay; no fixed amount is published, but immigration may ask.

declarations.name: Designated eVisa entry points
declarations.text: eVisa holders must enter through one of the designated airports or seaports (all major international airports qualify); exit is allowed through any authorised immigration checkpoint.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency over 5,000 USD in notes (or 10,000 USD total including instruments) must be declared on arrival. Bringing Indian rupees in is restricted for foreign visitors (25,000 INR limit).

source.name: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, India

notes: Duty-free allowance: 100 cigarettes, 2 litres of alcohol, gifts up to 50,000 INR.
Satellite phones are prohibited without a licence; drones require prior permission.

payments.text: Cards work in hotels, malls and city restaurants; small shops, rickshaws and rural areas are cash-first. UPI dominates local payments — foreign visitors can register for UPI with some providers.

safety.text: Most visits are trouble-free, but petty crime, traffic and scams around tourist sites warrant increased caution. Women travellers should take particular care, especially at night. Avoid border areas with Pakistan and parts of the northeast.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — India Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: October to March is dry and comfortable across most of the country; the Himalayan north is best May–September.

tips.text: Apply only at indianvisaonline.gov.in — look-alike sites charge large markups and some are outright scams.
Carry a printed copy of your eVisa approval (ETA) — airlines and immigration ask for it.
Some regions (parts of the northeast, Andaman & Nicobar tribal areas, border zones) require special permits beyond your visa.
Drink only bottled or purified water and ease into street food — stomach upsets are the most common traveller ailment.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for India?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a visa for India; most tourists use the e-Tourist Visa (30 days, 1 year or 5 years), applied for online at indianvisaonline.gov.in. Apply at least 4 days before travel.

faq.question: How much does an India eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The 30-day e-Tourist Visa has a standard fee of 25 USD (10 USD for April–June arrivals), the 1-year version 40 USD, and the 5-year version 80 USD. Fees differ for a few nationalities — the official portal shows your exact fee before payment.

faq.question: How long does the India eVisa take?
faq.answer: Most eVisas are approved within 1–4 business days. Apply at least 4 days before your flight; you cannot use the eVisa scheme more than twice per calendar year for the 30-day version.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations to enter India?
faq.answer: Only conditionally: a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from a risk country (strictly enforced — quarantine applies without it), and a polio vaccination certificate if arriving from a polio-affected country. No vaccinations are required when flying directly from Europe, the Americas or most of Asia.

faq.question: Can I extend an India eVisa?
faq.answer: Tourist eVisas cannot be extended. For longer stays, use the 1-year or 5-year multiple-entry eVisa (max 90 days per visit for most nationalities) or a regular embassy visa.
